Polling pressure from One Nation dominated the election coverage, with the AFR reporting the party polling beyond 20 seats and the Illawarra Mercury reporting Labor MPs bracing for a new "political reality" in seats including Kiama. Chris Minns also warned an expected Reserve Bank rate rise would permanently close shops, as NSW Treasury modelling pointed to the state's sensitivity to rate increases.
briefing.localWatch: The Illawarra Mercury reports One Nation could take up to 27 per cent of the vote in Labor strongholds such as Kiama and Shellharbour, and that Chris Minns has pledged a $6.8 billion South Coast rail upgrade that ministers warn will bring commuter disruption. Regional health is also in focus, with the Mercury reporting more than 130 people stranded amid an Illawarra hospital crisis and a new fast-track surgery service at Shellharbour Hospital.

stories.headline: Surging One Nation vote could mean new 'political reality' in Labor's Illawarra fortress: MPs
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that One Nation could win up to 27 per cent of the vote in NSW Labor strongholds including Kiama and Shellharbour, and that MPs say this could mean a new "political reality" in the region. The paper reports party insiders are planning how to respond.

stories.headline: No pain, no gain: how billion-dollar South Coast rail upgrades will create commuter disruption
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Premier Chris Minns has pledged a $6.8 billion upgrade of the South Coast rail line, including electrification. According to the report, ministers have warned the works will inevitably disrupt commuters.

stories.headline: Illawarra hospital crisis hits 'unprecedented' level with more than 130 people stranded
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports an "unprecedented" level of pressure on Illawarra hospitals, with more than 130 people stranded. No further detail was available in the supplied text.

stories.headline: NSW council refuses to show world-renowned Gaza artwork over ‘unacceptable’ safety risk
stories.summary: The Guardian reports exclusively that Shoalhaven City Council has declined to display the "Wall of Tears" installation by artist Phil Buehler. The council says the work posed a risk to staff, visitors and tenants.

stories.headline: Shellharbour Hospital's plan to fast-track surgeries and ease region waitlist times
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Shellharbour Hospital has introduced a high-volume short-stay surgery service. The service is part of a NSW government plan to reduce elective surgery waiting lists.

stories.headline: Emergency dashboard to find order in the chaos
stories.summary: Eurobodalla Shire Council has published an announcement about an emergency dashboard. No further detail was supplied beyond the council's headline.

stories.headline: Labor overhauls NSW playbook as One Nation polls beyond 20 seats
stories.summary: The Australian Financial Review reports One Nation is polling at a level that puts more than 20 seats in play, prompting Labor to rework its approach. According to the AFR, the Minns government plans an offensive in Liberal-held inner-suburban Sydney seats while defending its industrial heartland.

stories.headline: Diamonds, One Nation and a Bondi Rescue star: Inside Kellie Sloane’s campaign launch
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports on the campaign launch of Liberal MP Kellie Sloane. Only the headline was available in the supplied text.

stories.headline: National Gun Buyback in NSW begins today, industry support grants open
stories.summary: The Minns government says the biggest gun buyback in 30 years started in NSW on Monday, with the first firearms surrendered and industry support grants opening; the government frames it as a commitment to reduce the number of guns in the community. News.com.au reports more than 2000 firearms were due to be handed in on day one of the scheme, announced after the Bondi terror attack, and that critics have described it as a "PR exercise". The ABC reports only NSW and the ACT have so far joined the national scheme and that bookings at the six participating police stations are full, while 7NEWS reports hundreds of gun owners have signed up and The Australian reports the Premier has said he is willing to take a political hit over the buyback.

stories.headline: Minns warns expected RBA rate rise will see ‘shops close that don’t reopen’ as pressure mounts on PM
stories.summary: The Guardian reports Premier Chris Minns has warned that an expected Reserve Bank rate rise would cause shop closures and job losses, with one Labor MP quoted as saying voter anger is already high ahead of the decision. News.com.au reports commentary on the Premier's call for governments to reduce expenditure.

stories.headline: ‘Significant risks’: Medicos’ warning to Minns on pharmacist prescribing
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports five medical organisations have jointly asked the Premier to pause the planned expansion of pharmacist prescribing powers. The groups cite public safety grounds, according to the report.

stories.headline: 'Thinking with a pencil critical': Experts back NAPLAN test change
stories.summary: The ABC reports the NSW government wants NAPLAN testing returned to pen and paper from 2028, aiming to address a national decline in writing skills. Experts quoted by the ABC support the change.

stories.headline: As CBD high-rise developments creep south, this 101-year-old station needs an upgrade
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports the NSW government has announced a multimillion-dollar accessibility overhaul of Coniston station, including two lifts.

stories.headline: Building a mentally fit future for regional kids
stories.summary: The Minns government says it is providing $450,000 to extend Gotcha4Life's Mentally Fit Schools program to 20 regional primary schools, aimed at building children's resilience skills.

stories.headline: ‘Dropped the ball’: What ‘mediocre’ Melbourne has over ‘sexy’ Sydney
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports business leaders are urging NSW to use a major events fund to secure NFL and football events. The full article text was not available.

stories.headline: One Nation could stumble on its own sword
stories.summary: The AFR argues One Nation's success has rested on attacking what it calls the "uniparty", and that broadening its appeal to middle-ground voters could weaken that anti-establishment positioning.

stories.headline: The reason why a rate rise will hurt Sydneysiders most
stories.summary: The Herald examines NSW Treasury modelling which, it reports, finds the state is "particularly sensitive" to interest rate increases.

elsewhere.text: Victoria heads towards its state election, with Labor seeking a fourth consecutive term and the coalition hoping to turn the tide.
